title: US-Iran Nuclear MOU Remains Unsigned Week 15 of Hormuz Closure; Negotiators Continue Working Toward Deal; AU-ECOWAS Africa Peace Summit Announced for June 11-12
detail: June 5, 2026 — The US-Iran nuclear and Hormuz memorandum of understanding tentatively agreed by negotiators (confirmed CNN May 28) remains unsigned as the Strait of Hormuz enters its 15th week of closure. US and Iranian working-level teams continued exchanges through General Asim Munir of Pakistan as principal back-channel intermediary. Just Security's Early Edition on June 5 confirmed active negotiations are ongoing with the core framework (Phase 1: Hormuz reopens + US naval blockade lifted + Iran oil sales resume; Phase 2: 60-day nuclear talks on enrichment and HEU disposal) still the operative basis. PBS NewsHour confirmed that US and Iranian negotiators reached a 'tentative deal to extend ceasefire and start new nuclear talks' — but Trump's formal signing remains pending amid Congressional opposition from 52 senators and 177 House members. Al Jazeera's June 5 analysis asked 'If ceasefires are in place, why do strikes continue?' — examining the Lebanon-Israel and Gaza contexts alongside the Hormuz stalemate as part of a broader pattern of agreed frameworks being outrun by on-the-ground military dynamics. Iran briefly suspended negotiations on June 1 over Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza, adding procedural complication before resuming contact. US gasoline prices hold at approximately $4.48-4.50/gallon; Brent crude in $78-82/bbl range. Separately, the African Union Peace and Security Council Committee of Experts met on June 5 in preparation for the AU-ECOWAS 3rd Annual Joint Consultative Meeting scheduled for June 11-12 in Abuja, Nigeria — which will review governance, peace, and security across West Africa including Sahel peace processes and joint commitments from 2024-2025. Colombia's runoff preparations continue with June 21 as the next decisive date for the Americas peace landscape.

title: Gaza: Ceasefire Technically In Force but Violated 3,000+ Times Since October 2025; Israel Kills 11 June 4-5; Phase 2 Negotiations Stalled; UNSC Calls for Full Implementation
detail: June 5, 2026 — The Gaza ceasefire framework (in force since October 10, 2025) continues to exist on paper but remains under severe strain, with Israeli forces killing at least 11 Palestinians in fresh strikes on June 4-5 according to Drop Site News and Gaza health officials. Al Jazeera documented 3,005+ Israeli ceasefire violations between October 10, 2025 and May 27, 2026 — an average of approximately 4+ violations per day during a period nominally governed by a ceasefire. The UN Security Council held a briefing in early June calling the ceasefire 'far from perfect' but urging all parties to work toward full implementation. 77% of Gaza's population faces acute food insecurity according to OCHA; 80% of buildings have been damaged or destroyed. Phase 2 negotiations — which were to address Israeli troop withdrawal from Gaza and Hamas disarmament — remain entirely stalled: Israel has not withdrawn forces and effectively controls more than 50% of the Strip; Hamas has conditioned any disarmament discussion on a Palestinian statehood guarantee, which Israel rejects. The National Transitional Committee (ex-PA minister Ali Shaath, Board of Peace supervised) continues as a parallel governance track. Hezbollah's June 4 rejection of the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire framework has complicated the broader regional peace architecture, with Hezbollah stating its operations remain linked to Palestinian solidarity. The UN Security Council, with Colombia holding the June 2026 presidency, has a full peace-related agenda including UNDOF (Golan Heights) mandate renewal expiring June 30, Yemen Special Envoy Hans Grundberg's briefing, and an open debate on Women, Peace and Security.
